# Object Decomposition and Composition

Also called: Object Decomposition, Compositional NeRF, Scene Decomposition

## Overview
Object Decomposition and Composition refers to a family of [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) architectures that explicitly separate a scene into distinct semantic or geometric entities (objects) to enable instance-level editing, manipulation, and analysis. Unlike [standard NeRFs](#979-nerf-volumetric-rendering-coarse-fine-sampling.md) that treat the scene as a monolithic volume, these methods introduce mechanisms to identify, isolate, and recombine individual objects. This family is distinguished from siblings like [Signed Distance Function (SDF) Representations](12495-signed-distance-function-sdf-representations.md) by its focus on semantic/instance separation rather than just boundary representation, and from [Mixture-of-Experts and Modular Architectures](14429-mixture-of-experts-and-modular-architectures.md) by its specific goal of compositional [scene editing](#17595-scene-editing.md) rather than just computational efficiency.

## Shared principles
The core task of a NeRF [network architecture](#15530-network-architectures.md) is to learn a continuous volumetric scene representation $F_\Theta: (\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d}) \rightarrow (\sigma, \mathbf{c})$, where $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^3$ is the spatial position, $\mathbf{d} \in \mathbb{R}^3$ is the viewing direction, $\sigma$ is the volume density, and $\mathbf{c}$ is the view-dependent color. The rendering process integrates these outputs along rays using [standard volume rendering equations](#1165-standard-volume-rendering-equation.md).

## Subtopics

### [DM-NeRF](13525-dm-nerf.md)
Simultaneously reconstructs geometry, decomposes objects, and supports manipulation via a learnable object field.

### [Unified Decompositional and Compositional NeRF](14413-unified-decompositional-and-compositional-nerf.md)
Two-stage framework using a coarse global field to guide a fine-grained decomposed field, re-composed via differentiable one-hot weights.

### [Detail-based Segmentation](15935-detail-based-segmentation.md)
Divides scenes by object detail frequency, assigning high-frequency objects to individual NeRFs and low-frequency ones to a joint NeRF.

### Fig-NeRF
- [S1] [Scene composition](#11397-scene-composition.md) model for object interpolation and amodal segmentation using two separate NeRF models for foreground and background.
- [S1] Use an appearance NeRF conditioned on latent codes for the background model.
- [S1] Use two photometric losses, one for the foreground and one for the background.

## Background
The concept of decomposing scenes into compositional parts emerged early in NeRF research. [Fig-NeRF](#12006-fig-nerf.md) (April 2021) [S1] focused on object interpolation and amodal segmentation using separate NeRFs for foreground and background. [Object-NeRF](#11987-object-nerf.md) (September 2021) [S1] introduced a hybrid voxel-based approach with separate NeRFs for objects and the scene, conditioned on interpolated voxel features. These works laid the groundwork for later methods that integrate [decomposition](#7254-decomposition.md) directly into the optimization loop for editing.
